content:
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
Rotterdam, Netherlands | samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with experience operating Azure environments, developing Terraform modules for cloud networking, and automating application release pipelines. Background includes administering Windows and Linux servers, leading an on-premises-to-Azure migration, and implementing practical security baselines for small businesses.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD / Entra ID, Azure Monitor)
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Bash, Azure DevOps Pipelines
Systems and platforms: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Docker, Kubernetes (AKS), Ansible
Networking and security: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, MFA, conditional access
Administration: Active Directory, Microsoft 365 administration

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V., Rotterdam
Mar 2025 – Present
- Part of a three-person cloud team operating the company’s Azure estate, comprising approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions.
- Developed Terraform modules for landing-zone networking, including hub-and-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall, and private endpoints.
- Migrated release pipelines for 15 internal applications from manual deployments to Azure DevOps YAML pipelines.

Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed (Small Businesses)
Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
- Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
- Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Set up backups and basic security baselines, including MFA and conditional access.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, Schiedam
Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
- Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
- Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS in 2019.
- Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
- Provided second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.

Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011 – Dec 2013

EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College, 2011

CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025

LANGUAGES
Dutch (native), English (fluent), Twi (spoken)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and easy to scan. It presents credible scale through figures such as 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 application pipelines, 250 servers, and 60 migrated servers. The career progression from helpdesk through systems administration to cloud engineering is clear, and the contract and freelance experience is relevant to a contractor role. The main content weakness is that several job-relevant capabilities are either not evidenced or are only implied, particularly systems architecture, stakeholder leadership, and technical communication. There is also one unsupported skill entry that should be corrected.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, simple text formatting, and ATS-friendly keyword groupings. It should parse reliably and has strong keyword coverage for Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, Linux, virtual machines, networking, security, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code. AI screening probability is moderate to high for Azure-focused infrastructure roles, but lower for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, system design, or stakeholder-management evidence. These absent technologies and experiences must not be added unless truthful. The Azure AD / Entra ID wording is useful, although the skills section could be prioritized more closely around infrastructure engineering, cloud design, Terraform, networking, and security.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is hands-on cloud infrastructure operation and design: the candidate operates a substantial Azure estate, develops Terraform networking modules, manages VMs and AKS, and has led an Azure IaaS migration. Practical security awareness is shown through MFA, conditional access, backups, Azure Firewall, and private endpoints. Linux and virtual machines are clearly shown. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background because the advertisement states that AWS is preferred but other major clouds are acceptable. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/JVM development, or explicit systems-architecture and system-design work. The CV shows technical leadership through the server migration, but does not demonstrate leading proposals across stakeholders or agreeing interfaces with external engineering teams. The contractor background is relevant to the engagement model.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the CORE SKILLS section under "Cloud infrastructure," remove "Azure Monitor" because it does not appear in the Original Candidate Information. Keep the supported Azure technologies, including VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, and Azure AD / Entra ID.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE: In the PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY section, make the supported infrastructure-design and operating experience more explicit without adding unsupported claims. For example, change the opening to: "Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience operating Azure environments, designing cloud networking with Terraform, and automating application release pipelines." Retain the supported Windows/Linux administration, Azure IaaS migration, and security-baseline experience.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE: In the CORE SKILLS section, reorder the categories so the most relevant searchable terms appear first: "Infrastructure as code and automation," "Cloud infrastructure," "Networking and security," then "Systems and platforms" and "Administration." This will foreground Terraform, Bicep, Azure DevOps Pipelines, Azure networking, firewalls, MFA, and conditional access for infrastructure/DevOps screening.

MINOR: In the PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE section under "Systems Administrator," revise the migration bullet to use the job-relevant architecture and infrastructure terminology that is supported by the source material: "Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS in 2019." Do not describe this as broader systems architecture or stakeholder leadership unless the candidate can substantiate those activities.

MINOR: In the PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE section under "Cloud Engineer," retain the quantified scope and make the infrastructure-engineering wording more ATS-readable by changing "Part of a three-person cloud team operating the company’s Azure estate" to "Worked in a three-person cloud team operating the company’s Azure infrastructure estate." This preserves the facts while matching the advertisement's infrastructure-operation terminology.
critique.critical_issues: Potential hallucination: "Azure Monitor" appears in the CV's Core Skills section but is not present in the Original Candidate Information. Remove it unless the candidate can verify that they have used it.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professionally structured CV with strong quantitative evidence: approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 application pipelines, nine small-business clients, 250 servers, and a 60-server Azure migration. The summary is relevant and the experience is concise without unnecessary detail. The main content limitation is that it presents strong Azure operations experience but provides little evidence of broader systems architecture, stakeholder communication, observability, or technical proposal leadership. The current role is also relatively recent, so the CV should rely on precise scope and outcomes rather than implying experience that is not documented.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, readable date ranges, conventional job titles, and relevant keywords such as Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, networking, MFA, and conditional access. It should parse reliably and has a good screening probability for Azure-focused infrastructure roles. Its match probability for this specific vacancy is reduced by the absence of AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, system design, observability, and stakeholder-facing terminology. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than formatting defects, so unsupported keywords must not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly supports hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud environment operation, Terraform-based networking, Linux and virtual-machine administration, and practical security awareness. The Azure Firewall, private endpoints, MFA, conditional access, and Azure IaaS migration experience are relevant to the role's secure and reliable platform focus. The candidate's material does not establish Terragrunt, AWS, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/JVM development, or explicit stakeholder alignment. The CV does show leadership of a substantial infrastructure migration, but it does not demonstrate leading technical proposals across teams or bringing external stakeholders along. Alignment is therefore credible for the infrastructure portion of the role but limited for the fleet-connectivity and secure-device-communication aspects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary section, make the role's supported terminology more explicit by changing the opening to: "Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on infrastructure engineering experience designing and operating Azure cloud environments, developing Terraform networking modules, and automating application release pipelines." Keep the existing Windows/Linux administration, Azure migration, and practical security content after this sentence.
2. In the Core Skills section under "Cloud infrastructure," add "Azure Monitor" because it appears in the original candidate information and is relevant to the job's requirement for an observable, reliable platform. For example: "Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure Monitor, Azure AD / Entra ID)."
3. In the Professional Experience section under Havenstad Logistics B.V., replace "Worked in a three-person cloud team operating the company’s Azure infrastructure estate" with "Operated the company’s Azure infrastructure estate as part of a three-person cloud team." This uses the job description's infrastructure-operation language more directly without overstating individual ownership.
4. In the Professional Experience section under Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, retain and foreground the existing leadership evidence by changing the migration bullet to: "Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS in 2019." This is more direct and makes the strongest available evidence of technical leadership easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.
5. Do not add AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, automotive systems, backend/JVM development, or stakeholder-management claims unless they are supported by additional factual experience. The current CV should remain a truthful Azure/Terraform infrastructure profile.
